candidates.exact_span:
EPA-approved test procedures (methods) for the analysis and quantification of pollutants or
pollutant parameters, including for the purposes of compliance monitoring/DMR reporting, permit
renewal applications, or any other reporting that may be required as a condition of this permit,
shall be sufficiently sensitive.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Scopes which reporting contexts trigger the sensitivity requirement; different readings of 'compliance monitoring/DMR reporting' versus 'any other reporting' could change which measurements are subject to MQL-based compliance evaluation (A), which monitoring/reporting obligations apply (B), and how missing or non-numeric results are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span:
the method minimum
level (ML) of quantification is at or below the level of the applicable effluent limit for the measured
pollutant or pollutant parameter
candidates.computation_change_reason: Criterion (1) ties method quantification to the 'applicable effluent limit'; interpretation of which limit is applicable, or whether ML is at or below that limit, could change whether a numeric compliance comparison is feasible and whether reported values below the ML are treated as exceeding, meeting, or not comparable to the limit.

candidates.exact_span:
if there is no EPA-approved analytical method with a
published ML at or below the effluent limit (see table below), then the method has the lowest
published ML (is the most sensitive) of the analytical methods approved under 40 CFR Part 136
or required under 40 CFR Chapter I, Subchapters N or 0, for the measured pollutant or pollutant
parameter
candidates.computation_change_reason: When no published method meets the effluent limit, the operative standard shifts to the most sensitive approved method rather than direct limit comparison; different interpretations of 'no EPA-approved analytical method' or which methods count under 40 CFR Part 136 / Subchapters N or O could change applicable limits (A), required monitoring methods (B), and how sub-ML or non-detect results are semantically classified (C).

candidates.exact_span:
the method is specified in this permit or has been otherwise approved in writing
by the permitting authority (EPA Region 6) for the measured pollutant or pollutant parameter
candidates.computation_change_reason: Permit-specified or Region 6–approved methods can establish an alternative quantification threshold; whether such approval exists or applies to a given parameter could change which numeric limit governs compliance (A), which monitoring method is required (B), and whether missing evidence reflects an approved alternative ML or an unresolved obligation (C).

candidates.exact_span:
The Permittee has the option of developing and submitting a report to justify the use of matrix or
sample-specific MLs rather than the published levels. Upon written approval by EPA Region 6 the
matrix or sample-specific MLs may be utilized by the Permittee for all future Discharge
Monitoring Report (DMR) reporting requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Written approval of matrix- or sample-specific MLs can replace published MQLs for future DMR reporting; whether such approval exists and is in effect could change the effective comparison level for limits (A), ongoing DMR monitoring obligations (B), and whether absent or below-threshold data reflects a documented no-data state versus inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span:
Current EPA Region 6 minimum quantification levels (MQLs) for reporting and compliance are
provided in Appendix A of Part II of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Appendix A is referenced as the source of operative MQL values used for both reporting and compliance; interpretation of which appendix values apply, or how 'reporting' versus 'compliance' MQLs are distinguished, could change limit-exceedance determinations (A), applicable monitoring/reporting requirements (B), and classification of results relative to required detection levels (C).

candidates.exact_span: The following pollutants may not have EPA approved methods with a published ML at or below the effluent limit, if specified:
candidates.computation_change_reason: The conditional phrase 'if specified' governs which pollutants are subject to the no-method-at-or-below-limit pathway; different readings of what must be 'specified' (permit text, appendix, effluent limit table, or other condition) could change whether criterion (2) applies and thereby alter limit comparisons (A), monitoring method requirements (B), and missing-evidence handling for those parameters (C).
